page: OVHcloud c3-320 is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance allocates 160 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core), presenting 160 vCPUs alongside 320 GB of system memory. This configuration adheres to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB of RAM per core). In addition to compute resources, the server includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are bundled.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded execution capabilities. The 160 dedicated cores yield exceptional performance across parallelized benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 116,050.79, multi-core stress-ng throughput of 288,128.15, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 1,240.95 GB/sec. Parallelized software compilation under Clang (73,612.0) and ray tracing tasks (127,265.0) both place within the top 10% of tested instances. Redis SET throughput is notably elevated at 173.62 million operations per second.

Single-core performance falls in the average to strong tiers, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,917.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 29.13 GB/sec. Additionally, instruction set support lacks AVX-512 extensions and AMX units, which limits acceleration for specialized matrix operations and yields average execution metrics for larger LLM generation tasks. The 400 GB local NVMe volume offers fast low-latency scratch space, though high-capacity persistent storage must be handled separately.

OVHcloud c3-320 is best deployed for high-density, multi-core parallel workloads. Typical applications include large-scale CI/CD software compilation pipelines, CPU-based rendering and physics simulations, distributed caching nodes, batch processing, and high-concurrency stateless web services.

It features 320 GB of RAM, a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 20 Gbps baseline network link. Across synthetic and practical benchmarks, the system delivers top-tier parallel compute metrics, evidenced by superior scores in Clang compilation, ray tracing, multi-core stress tests, and Redis operations. Single-thread processing registers at an average level, and the architecture does not support AVX-512 extensions. Given its dense dedicated core layout and high memory bandwidth, the instance is well suited for CPU rendering, continuous integration build clusters, parallel scientific computing, and high-throughput distributed caching workloads.
